Nawaz urges unity after Naqvi’s system remarks

Published on: August 4, 2026 12:49 AM

Government

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:53
Instaread

Former prime minister Nawaz Sharif has advised senior Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) leaders to avoid making public statements about Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s recent remarks on the country’s “collapsed system.” He stressed that Pakistan’s current economic, political and security challenges require strong cooperation among all state institutions. Nawaz also emphasised that no action should create the impression of differences between the federal government and the military leadership.

Geographic Reference

According to sources, Nawaz Sharif told party leaders that national interests must remain the top priority during this critical period. He highlighted the importance of maintaining close coordination between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir. He said institutional harmony and collective efforts are essential to address the country’s key challenges and ensure continued stability.

Meanwhile, several senior PML-N leaders reportedly shared concerns about Mohsin Naqvi’s public remarks. They believed that if the interior minister had concerns about governance or administrative weaknesses, he should have discussed them during federal cabinet meetings instead of raising them at a public event. They argued that describing the system as “collapsed” could unintentionally undermine the government’s efforts to improve governance.

Read more : Maryam Nawaz’s narrative triumphs in Azad Kashmir –

Some party leaders also felt the statement created an impression that meaningful reforms were impossible under the current administrative structure. They considered this perception politically harmful and believed it could weaken public confidence in the government’s performance. Despite these concerns, they avoided escalating the issue publicly in line with Nawaz Sharif’s instructions to maintain party discipline and institutional unity.

Computer Science

However, sources strongly rejected speculation about any disagreement between Islamabad and Rawalpindi. They said the civil and military leadership remain fully aligned on major national priorities, including economic recovery, national security, investment promotion and governance reforms. According to the sources, both sides continue to work closely together, and there is no indication of any confrontation or institutional rift.
